$comment: Profile definitions for setup.mjs. Globs relative to payload/. exclude wins over include; extends unions the parent chain's exclude first. optional groups are promoted over exclude when active.
$marketplaces: Where each managed plugin's marketplace comes from, so setup.mjs can register it before installing - `claude plugin install` fails outright against an unknown marketplace. Sources are transcribed from a real ~/.claude/plugins/known_marketplaces.json, not guessed; a marketplace with no entry here produces a note telling the human to add one, never an invented repo. This gap predates the fork: the four pre-fork plugins live in marketplaces that any machine which ran the bootstrap already has, so nothing ever tripped it.
$gsd: Forbidden because GSD left the bundle in phase 26. `gsd` stays in managedPlugins so plugin-reconcile uninstalls it from a machine that still has it; no profile lists it.
$context7: Forbidden, not merely unrequired. Context7 is reached through its MCP server; the marketplace plugin of the same name shadows that, so it is removed on sight rather than left disabled. It stays in managedPlugins because a plugin nobody manages is a plugin nobody can find and remove.
$forbiddenPlugins: Must not exist on the machine at all. Stronger than absence from a profile: plugin-reconcile refuses to install or enable these no matter what a profile asks for, ignores keepInstalled for them, and uninstalls (removes files) rather than disabling. Every name here must also be in managedPlugins, and no profile may list one - both are asserted in variants.test.mjs.
$keepInstalled: Managed plugins that are disabled when not required, but never uninstalled. superpowers is here because ultrapowers is our fork of it: keeping upstream on disk makes rollback one command (re-enable it, disable the fork) instead of a reinstall from the marketplace. It must stay in managedPlugins to be disabled at all - a plugin we stop managing is a plugin we stop turning off. Both enabled at once is NOT the fallback: they share 14 skill names and that is undocumented behaviour we do not run in production. ultrapowers is here for `lite`, which ships it to disk but does not enable it.
$sessionDefaults: Keys setup.mjs manages in ~/.claude/settings.json on every profile. Absent: written. Different: a conflict - written under --replace-all or an interactive yes, otherwise printed.
$managedMcpServers: User-scope MCP servers setup.mjs may add or remove. A profile lists the ones it wants in mcpServers (absent: inherited through extends); a configured server is never rewritten. headerFromEnv maps a header to the environment variable holding its value - values never live here. postAdd runs once, right after a successful add, under the same consent.

context7.missingEnvNote: CONTEXT7_API_KEY not set - registered without a key (lower rate limit)

deepseek.missingEnvNote: LLM_KEY not set - DeepSeek tools register but return unavailable until it is set

$deepseekDefaults: Default offload level written to ~/.claude/deepseek-defaults.json per installed profile; the per-project .claude/deepseek.json overrides it, down to off. {{CLAUDE_DIR}} in a managedMcpServers arg is substituted by setup.mjs to the absolute config dir. See phase 25.
